obs: "Kentucky, like most States, regards only the lender as the usurer, and the borrower as the victim. See Ky. Rev. Stat. 360.020 (1987) (lender liable to borrower for civil penalty), 360.990 (lender guilty of misdemeanor). Since the Kentucky statute imposed no penalties upon the borrower... but to the contrary enabled him to pay back the principal without any interest, and to sue for double the amount of interest already paid..."

"Moreover, the fact that the Sherman Act authorizes the recovery of treble damages and attorneys fees for successful plaintiffs indicates that Congress intended to encourage, rather than discourage, private enforcement of the law."
